en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is renowned for its nearly perfect conical shape among all Philippine volcanoes.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the entire Philippines.
Lake Taal is a unique freshwater lake located entirely within the massive volcanic caldera of Batangas.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines with an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The critically endangered Philippine Eagle is a large bird of prey endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Verde Island Passage, located between Batangas and Mindoro, is recognized as the center of global marine shorefish biodiversity.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains were carved into the steep slopes by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
Baguio City, situated in the Cordillera mountains at an elevation of 1,500 meters, experiences a much cooler climate than lowland areas.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, located in the Sulu Sea, is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral atolls.
The San Bernardino Strait is a vital waterway that separates the Bicol Peninsula of Luzon from the island of Samar.
